content.learning_goal: Enable Grade 7 learners to understand and apply the central ideas of Earth, Moon, and the Sun.

explanation_sections.title: Activate
explanation_sections.explanation: Connect the chapter to prior knowledge, observation or experience.

explanation_sections.title: Build
explanation_sections.explanation: Teach from the source-grounded points and examples.
source_evidence: Earth, Moon, and 12 the Sun One morning in Kanniyakumari, Tamil Nadu, 12-year-old Rashmika was eagerly cycling to school.
That was the day her science teacher had dedicated a class for students to share and try to explain interesting observations.
Rashmika had been noticing that the coconut tree shadows were long in the morning but shorter in the afternoon on her way back.
She thought about it and decided that the size of the shadows changed because the Sun moved across the sky during the day.
But she also remembered learning that the Earth moved around the Sun (in chapter ‘Beyond Earth’ in the Grade 6 Science textbook Curiosity) so she was puzzled.

explanation_sections.title: Reason
explanation_sections.explanation: Ask learners to explain relationships, evidence, patterns or steps.

explanation_sections.title: Transfer
explanation_sections.explanation: Move from the textbook context to a closely related new situation.

misconceptions: Confusing an example with the underlying concept.
checks_for_understanding: What changes if an important condition changes?
content.closure: Learner states the central idea, supporting evidence and one application.
